# Protocol implementation guides

Rimsky orchestrates work by calling out to services you write. This set tells you how to write one.

Nine gRPC services live in ten `.proto` files, all in the protobuf package `rimsky.v1`. Pick the guide for the protocol you are implementing, then read the shared conventions page for the parts every service shares.

## Start here

- [Shared conventions](conventions.md) — the packages you import, the capabilities handshake, the HTTP+JSON bridge, mutual-TLS enrollment, TLS modes, and how a service is declared to a deployment. Read this first whichever protocol you implement.

## One guide per protocol

| Guide | Services covered | Rimsky's role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Executor](executor.md) | `Executor`, `ExecutorObservability` | Rimsky calls you to run a node |
| [Claim producer](claim-producer.md) | `ClaimProducer`, `ClaimProducerObservability` | Rimsky calls you to acquire and close claims |
| [Data processing](data-processing.md) | `DataProcessing` | Rimsky calls you to stage and promote data versions |
| [Publisher](publisher.md) | `Publisher` | Rimsky calls you to start and stop watches; you push messages back |
| [Lifecycle subscriber](lifecycle-subscriber.md) | `LifecycleSubscriber` | Rimsky calls you when templates and instances change |
| [Validation](validation.md) | `Validation` | Rimsky calls you at template registration |
| [Host daemon](host-daemon.md) | `HostDaemon` | You dial rimsky's proxy and hold the stream open |

An observability protocol is a sibling of its primary protocol, served by the same process on the same endpoint. Its guide is the primary protocol's guide.

## Reference pages

- [Event payloads](events.md) — `events.proto`, the tenth proto file. It declares no service. Read it if you consume rimsky's event log.
- [Conformance](conformance.md) — the eight `rimsky conformance` subcommands, what each proves, and the exit codes CI can read.

## Choosing a protocol

- Run work for a node: **Executor**.
- Hand a node exclusive access to something outside rimsky — a table, a folder, a capacity counter: **Claim producer**.
- Give a claim producer versioned staging and promotion: **Data processing**, as a mix-in on the claim producer.
- Wake instances from outside events — a schedule, a poll, a webhook: **Publisher**.
- React to templates being registered or instances being created: **Lifecycle subscriber**.
- Reject bad templates at registration rather than at dispatch: **Validation**, as a mix-in on any of the above.
- Run work on a developer's own machine: **Host daemon**.
